data.answer: Use `read_dotenv` from `dotenv`. It parses the file and returns a dict without touching `os.environ`. Pass a path, or a `stream`. If you pass neither, it uses `find_dotenv()` to locate the file. Keys with no value (a bare `FOO` line) come back as `None`. Interpolation of `${VAR}` is on by default, and you can turn it off with `interpolate=False`.
warnings: README.md 'Load configuration without altering the environment' (lines 80-104) uses `dotenv_values`. That function no longer exists. The code defines and exports `read_dotenv` instead, so `from dotenv import dotenv_values` will fail with ImportError. Use `read_dotenv`.
README.md line 107 ('Parse configuration as a stream') also refers to `dotenv_values`. Use `read_dotenv(stream=...)`.
